books.section: Topic 6.12 Controversies over the Role of Government in the Gilded Age

primary_sources: Joint resolution of Congress (Teller Amendment), April 20, 1898

stimulus.text:
Joint resolution of Congress, April 20, 1898 (the Teller Amendment):

“Fourth. That the United States hereby disclaims any disposition or intention to exercise sovereignty, jurisdiction, or control over said Island except for the pacification thereof, and asserts its determination, when that is accomplished, to leave the government and control of the Island to its people.”

The “Island” is Cuba. In the same year, 1898, the United States annexed Hawaii and, after the war with Spain, took Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines.
stimulus.source_note: Joint resolution approved April 20, 1898 (Teller Amendment). The quoted clause is exact. Hawaii was annexed by joint resolution in 1898; Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines were ceded by Spain in the Treaty of Paris, December 1898.

stem: Congress disclaimed empire in Cuba in April 1898, yet in the same year the United States annexed Hawaii and took Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines. What tension does that best show?

options.text: Americans agreed that the United States should take no overseas territory
options.misconception: Hawaii was annexed and three territories were taken, so Americans did not all agree.

options.text: Cuba was annexed along with Hawaii in 1898
options.misconception: Cuba was not annexed; the Teller Amendment promised to leave it to its people.

options.text: Spain kept all of its overseas empire after the war
options.misconception: Spain ceded Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines in 1898.

options.text: Americans were divided over becoming an imperial power

rationales.A: Hawaii was annexed and three territories taken, so agreement is false.
rationales.B: Cuba was not annexed; the amendment promised to leave it to its people.
rationales.C: Spain ceded Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines in 1898.
rationales.D: One act refused empire in Cuba while other acts took territory, showing division.
rationales.general:
Hold the two facts side by side.
1. In April 1898 Congress promised not to take Cuba for the United States.
2. In the same year the United States annexed Hawaii and took three Spanish territories.
3. The same nation refused empire in one place and took it in others.
4. The contradiction shows Americans divided over becoming an imperial power.
Remember: when one year holds opposite acts, the division is the point.
